deep-teal.$description: Deep Teal — Teal supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

ink.$description: Ink — Primary body text, headings, icon strokes, link text, and nav labels — a near-black that softens to charcoal, avoiding the harshness of pure black on warm white

canvas-warmth.$description: Canvas Warmth — Page background — a warm, paper-like off-white that gives the entire interface a human, editorial quality distinct from clinical SaaS whites

surface-white.$description: Surface White — Light supporting surface for subtle backgrounds and section separation. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

hairline.$description: Hairline — Subtle borders, dividers between content blocks, and input field outlines — light enough to recede but present enough to structure information

border-soft.$description: Border Soft — Supporting neutral for secondary UI, dividers, and muted labels. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

pure-black.$description: Pure Black — Reserved for icon fills and the rare element requiring maximum contrast — used sparingly alongside the softer Ink

teal-mist.$description: Teal Mist — Light teal-tinted surface for accent backgrounds, highlight panels, and soft washes that echo the brand color without dominating

blush-neutral.$description: Blush Neutral — Warm pink-tinted surface for category differentiation in editorial layouts — used as a subtle alternative to teal-tinted sections

n26.$description: The workhorse sans-serif for all navigation, body copy, buttons, labels, and UI micro-text. Weight 500 for emphasis, 700 for primary action labels and key headings. Slight positive tracking (0.008–0.019em) gives small sizes a controlled, legible quality — the custom feel comes from this restrained openness rather than display flourishes.

n26-extended.$description: Display face reserved for hero headlines, section titles, and large statement copy. The wider proportions at 58–80px create breathing room that contrasts the compact N26 body face — this duality (tight UI type + expansive display type) is the typographic signature. Normal letter-spacing lets the wide letterforms do the work.
